additional_info.body:
Hi Joseph,
Sorry for the delay in the message as it's been a busy morning. We found a problem in the CFAST, which we are not sure why it happened but having the charger offline all the time does not help finding the root cause.
I will support you in case you miss something from the guide below.
We have 2 options here:
Flash the 32GB USB with the image I sent you via email and restore the configuration
This option might not work since there is a problem with CFAST
To flash the USB follow this guide:
Get a USB stick (Size = 32 GB)
Plug in USB stick to your notebook
Flash the Live Linux image onto the USB Stick using Balena Etcher
Open
autorun
folder
Go to
scripts_NOT_to_run
Copy files you want to run to folder scripts_to_run - this case we want the Restore-config
create new folder
data
on USB drive
copy config files to USB drive in
data
boot charger from USB drive and follow the screen instructions
Shutdown charger
Unplug CFast Card
Plug in USB stick in -KF1’s USB port
Plug in your USB keyboard
Power on charger and wait for the Live Linux to automatically start
Observe charger UI, wait for the instruction to plug in CFast card. In some cases you might not be able to see the instructions as shown below. The waiting time depends on the script to run. Plug in the CFast card after the script-specific waiting time in case you don't see anything on the UI.
The charger will now boot from the CFast card. Wait until you see following screen.
​​​​​​​
​​​​​​​
Unplug USB stick and wait until booting is finished.
Open the CFAST card with a reader and delete a file on it:
Here is a link for CFAST card readers, since it's sold in Amazon I assume you can buy it locally in any tech store:
https://www.amazon.com/cfast-card-reader/s?k=cfast+card+reader
For this, we need to do it together.
I send the config files in attachment for the restore config, you just need to unzip the files on the data folder.
Let me know your feedback!
Thank you and it was great to hear from you again.
Best regards,
Francisco
